plain_rust_today: Clippy flags many of these, but only if enabled.
corten_mechanism: Lints enforced by the gate rather than opt-in (section 10)

plain_rust_today: Nothing in the language; authority is ambient (any code can open files, sockets, processes).
corten_mechanism: Capabilities passed in from a signed manifest; evidence types such as `Permission<Delete, Account>` (4.3, 4.11)

plain_rust_today: RAII and ownership manage most lifetimes; `mem::forget` and leaks are safe.
corten_mechanism: Linear handles, no `mem::forget`, compiler-supplied finalizers, quotas (4.1, 4.12)

plain_rust_today: Strings flow into SQL, HTML, shell and log sinks via `format!` with no checks.
corten_mechanism: Typed sinks only (`sql!`, `html!`, `process!`, `log_record!`); no raw constructors (4.5, 4.6)

plain_rust_today: `std::fs` opens any string path; no traversal or symlink protection.
corten_mechanism: `DirCap` + `PathSeg` on `openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH` and no symlinks (4.4)

plain_rust_today: `pub` fields, `static` items and ambient file and network access are all available.
corten_mechanism: No ambient authority, no mutable public statics, capability-scoped resources (4.3)

plain_rust_today: Safe Rust prevents use-after-free, double free and out-of-bounds access, but any crate may use `unsafe` or FFI.
corten_mechanism: No application `unsafe` or in-process FFI, enforced by the gate; foreign code isolated in Wasm or a process (4.1, 4.14)

plain_rust_today: `Command` can run a shell; query and template strings are plain `String`s.
corten_mechanism: No shell strings, no `eval`, no DTDs; context-typed sinks (4.5)

plain_rust_today: `#[derive(Debug)]` prints secrets; no data labels.
corten_mechanism: `Secret<T>` without `Debug`/`Display`, labelled errors, non-elidable wipe (4.9, 4.7)

plain_rust_today: `Send`/`Sync` already rule out data races in safe Rust; logical races, TOCTOU and deadlocks remain.
corten_mechanism: Structured concurrency, bounded channels, affine lock guards, `blocking` effect (4.8)

plain_rust_today: Exhaustive `match` prevents missing cases; panics and early returns can skip logic.
corten_mechanism: No exceptions or `finally`; must-use results; typestates for required order (4.7, 4.11)

plain_rust_today: No cryptography in `std`; safety depends on the crate chosen.
corten_mechanism: Goal-oriented crypto API: TLS 1.3, AEAD with managed nonces, no skip-verification (4.10)

plain_rust_today: No RNG in `std`; quality depends on the crate.
corten_mechanism: OS CSPRNG only, behind a `random` capability (4.10)

plain_rust_today: Nothing in the language.
corten_mechanism: Fail-closed defaults, `Secure`/`HttpOnly` cookies, refused operations on weak platforms (4.4, 4.6)

plain_rust_today: `PartialEq` can be derived for anything; no constant-time comparison in `std`.
corten_mechanism: Domain types instead of raw strings; constant-time comparison for secrets (4.5, 4.9)

plain_rust_today: No signing or verification in `std`.
corten_mechanism: Signed updates and manifests, typed trust stores (4.10, 4.15)

plain_rust_today: Nothing in the language.
corten_mechanism: Least authority by construction; the rest is design review (4.3, section 7)

plain_rust_today: No built-in notion of untrusted input.
corten_mechanism: `Untrusted<T>` parsed into domain types; refinements in decidable fragments (4.5, 4.13)

plain_rust_today: Integer overflow panics in debug builds but wraps in release by default; `as` truncates silently.
corten_mechanism: Checked arithmetic in every profile, no implicit casts, distinct wrapping types (4.2)

plain_rust_today: No quotas or budgets.
corten_mechanism: Mandatory budgets on parse, decode and allocate; per-component limits (4.12)

plain_rust_today: No checks on what crates or processes exchange.
corten_mechanism: Schema-checked broker IPC and declared effects per package (4.14, 4.15)

category: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
plain_rust_today: `Result` is `#[must_use]`, but `let _ =` discards it; `unwrap` and panics are common.
corten_mechanism: Linear must-use `Result`, exhaustive matching, supervision of panicked components (4.7)
